title.value: Discrete Factorial Representations as an Abstraction for Goal Conditioned RL
title.justification: The paper's title is "Discrete Factorial Representations as an Abstraction for Goal Conditioned RL," which is prominently displayed at the beginning of the provided document.
title.quote: Discrete Factorial Representations as an Abstraction for Goal Conditioned RL

extractions.description: The paper discusses a novel approach in reinforcement learning, specifically in goal-conditioned reinforcement learning (RL). It proposes to enhance generalization and goal grounding by leveraging discrete factorial representations, a process named DGRL. The method involves learning goal representations with self-supervised learning, followed by vector quantization to enforce a discrete bottleneck, thus improving goal specification and representation. The approach aims to improve RL agent performance in various tasks, from navigation to robotic manipulation, particularly focusing on generalization to goals not seen during training.

sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Goal-conditioned reinforcement learning (RL) is a promising direction for training agents that are capable of solving multiple tasks and reach a diverse set of objectives.

primary_category.quote: We propose to address this by learning factorial representations of goals and processing the resulting representation via a discretization bottleneck, for coarser goal specification, through an approach we call DGRL.

new_primary_category.quote: The effectiveness of goal-conditioned HRL relies on the specification of semantically meaningful sub-goals. Using factorial discrete sub-goals allows the higher-level policy to specify semantically meaningful objectives to the lower-level policy.
